source.title: Weight Concentration Regularization for Improving Pruning Robustness Under High Sparsity
source.authors: Vincent-Daniel Yun; Junhyuk Jo; Sun-Woo Lee

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies pruning robustness. Its generalization analysis reports validation accuracy and a curvature proxy, but does not measure the train–test gap or test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper's pruning results concern accuracy after pruning, not the claim's natural-label train–test generalization. Section 5.4 reports a generalization analysis, but it does not measure training error or a train–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study measures WCR's pruning robustness and its effects on validation accuracy and unscaled Hessian curvature. None tests V1–V8. In particular, V7 requires magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance related to train–test gaps; a principal Hessian eigenvalue paired with validation accuracy does not measure that relationship. The study also provides no controlled batch-size comparison for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that WCR improves one-shot pruning robustness across image classification, medical segmentation, and LoRA-based LLM fine-tuning, and composes with pruning-robust optimizers. Their separate CIFAR-10 analysis reports lower Hessian curvature alongside higher validation accuracy, suggesting an association with flatter solutions in that setting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains with a weight-concentration regularizer and evaluates post-training pruning; it does not test the listed memorization, architecture, optimizer-generalization, batch-size, dropout, sharpness-gap, or memorized-example claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization analysis varies optimizer (SGD or SAM), but gives no numerical values in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.4 and Figure 4 report that WCR lowers the principal Hessian eigenvalue and improves validation accuracy for CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 under SGD and SAM, using batch size 1024 and 300 epochs. Numerical values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding WCR is associated with lower unscaled Hessian curvature and higher validation accuracy in this particular training setting.

record.code_released: Official code repository will be released soon.
record.problems: The generalization analysis reports no numerical values in the text and no training-error or train–test-gap measure; Figure 4 is the only evidence for these results. Results are averaged over 3 random seeds in the classification tables, but uncertainty intervals are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Pruning accuracy tables and results are outside the claim's natural-label train–test generalization scope.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under comparable tuning; AdamW is used only in the separate LLM pipeline.
Held-out performance across controlled batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets and whether recipe changes remove a large-batch penalty.
Controlled dropout additions or removals and resulting held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of training-error measurements alone would not exclude tests of versions about held-out performance. Here, exclusion rests on the missing version-specific comparisons and measures. Pruning removes weights, not V8's memorized training examples; the pruning results are already declared outside scope in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons on held-out performance.
Batch-size effects on the train–test gap.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance and its relationship to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
